3010:

**of** or **for** λειτουργία, {{LXX|LXX.Exo.31.10, +others}}; ἡμέραι (in temples) {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“PTeb.” 88.6 (2nd c.BC)}}; **ministering**, πνεύματα {{NT|NT.Heb.1.14:}} _substantive_ -κόν (i.e. τέλος), τό, probably a tax paid in lieu of labour performed, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PPetr.” 2p.129 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 5.49 (2nd c.BC), +others}}:—in form **λειτουργιακός** {{Refs|“Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 7.209.19.}}
3012:

3026:
** λῆρος**, ὁ,
**A** **trash, trumpery**, of what is showy but useless, λήροις ἀναδῶν τοὺς νικῶντας {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 589; τραγικὸς λ. [prev. author] “Ra.” 1005}}; λῆρόν τε τἄλλ᾽ ἡγεῖτο τοῦ γνῶναι πέρι φύσεις ποιητῶν **no good** as connoisseurs of poets,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 809; λ. πάντα πρὸς τὸ χρυσίον 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 232.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.41}}; λ. εἶναι δοκεῖ τὸ νόμισμα, φύσει δ᾽ οὐθέν **mere trash**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1257b10}}; a mere **trifle**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 72c, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 60}}; λ. ἐστι τἄλλα πρὸς Κινησίαν there's **naught** to compare with Cinesias, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 860}}; οἱ ποιηταὶ λ. εἰσιν **useless, futile**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Xenarchus Comicus 7.1; ποιητῶν λ. 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 306; ἐμὲ μὲν λ. ἡγεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 176a, compare “Tht.” 176d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 10.3; λεπτοτάτων λ. ἱερεῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 359}}; λῆροι καὶ παιδιαί, of flute-playing at banquets, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 347d}}; λῆροι καὶ φλυαρίαι **futile** nonsense, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Hp.Ma.” 304b; ὁδοὺς καὶ κρήνας καὶ λήρους 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.29}}; παροψίδες καὶ λῆρος side-dishes and suchlike **trumpery**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 261.5; παρεὶς λ. πολὺν ἀστακὸν ὠνοῦ 4th c.BC: Archestratus Epicus “fragment” 24, compare 35.7}}; as an exclamation, λῆρος **nonsense! humbug**! {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 23, compare 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 41.8.}}
**A.2** **delirium**, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.26.γ (as variant for{παράληρος}).}}]
**A.II** as _adjective_, **silly**, ποιητής {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Gall.” 6, compare “Rh.Pr.” 17}}. _adverb_ -ρως [{{Refs|12th c.AD: Tzetzes, Joannes Grammaticus “Historiarum variarum chiliades” 13.337. (Perh. derived from {λῆρος})}}]
3032:
** λῑβερτῖνος**, ὁ,
= Latin _libertinus, freedman,_ {{NT|Inscriptiones Graecae 14.1781, NT.Act.6.9}}:—also **λίβερτος**, = Latin _libertus_, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.18.4.}}
3033:
** Λῐβύη** [ῠ], ἡ,
{{Refs 8th c.BC+|“Libya”, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.85, 14.295, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.46, etc.; also for “Africa” generally, [prev. author] 4.42, +others}}; **the west bank of the Nile,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|PTaur. 8.9 (2nd c.BC), “PLond.” 1.3.8 (2nd c.BC): proverbial, ἀεὶ Λιβύη φέρει τι καινόν or κακόν, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 606b20, 2nd c.AD: Zenobius Paroemiographus 2.51}}:— _adverb_ **Λῐβύηθεν**, **from Libya**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 46, 222}}:—also **Λῐβύηθε**, _Doric dialect_ **Λῐβῠ-ᾱθε**, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 368, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.24}}:— _adjective_ **Λῐβῠκός**, ή, όν, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8, etc.}}; Λ. ὄρνεον, i.e. a **strange, foreign** bird, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 65}}; Λ. λόγοι a kind of fables resembling those of Aesop, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1393a30}}; also, **western**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 119}}; ={δυτικός}, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Paraphrasis Ptolemaei Tetrabiblou” 29.}}
3035:
** λῐθ-ῐνος**, η, ον,
also ος, ον {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“Anthologia Graeca” 9.719, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.33}}:— **made of stone**, {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 10, 6th c.BC: Ibycus Lyricus 22, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.88, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.109, “PHib.” 1.27.26 (3rd c.BC), etc.}}; λ. θάνατος, i.e. caused by seeing the {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Gorgon 's head, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.48; so λ. εὐθὺς γίγνομαι 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 166.4}}; but, ἕστηκε λίθινος, of a statue, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.141 (compare ἵστημι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.2)}}; τὰ λ. **marble statues**, [{{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 3.5; Ἑρμῆς λ. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 96; for 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.69, see at {λίθος} 11.1, ὕαλος 11: _metaphorically_, καρδία LXX.Eze.11.19}}]. _adverb_ -νως **like stone**, λ. βλέπειν πρός τινα, with allusion to the {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Gorgon, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.24.}}
3036:
** λῐθοβολ-έω**,
**pelt with stones, stone**, {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Lev.20.2, +others, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.41, NT.Matt.21.35, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1011e}}:—_passive_, {{LXX|LXX.Exo.8.26(22).}}
3039:
** λικμ-άω**,
_future_ -ήσω {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 18.8}}: _aorist_ ἐλίκμησα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus “fragment” 34}}:— **part the grain from the chaff, winnow**, ἀνδρῶν λικμώντων {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.500; σῖτον λ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 18.6}}; καρπὸν ἀπ᾽ ἀσταχύων B.[same place]: _metaphorically_, **scatter like chaff**, {{LXX|LXX.Eze.29.12}}; **make away with**,{{LXX|LXX.Isa.30.22}}; **crush, destroy**, ἐλίκμησάν μου τὸ λάχανον {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“BGU” 146.8 (3rd c.AD)}}; ἐφ᾽ ὃν δ᾽ ἂν πέσῃ (i.e. ὁ λίθος) λικμήσει αὐτόν {{NT|NT.Luke.20.18.}}
3044:
** Λίνος** [ῐ], ὁ,
“Linos”, a mythical minstrel, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 192, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.105, 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 1.3.2}}.
**II** as _appellative_, **the song** or **lay of Linos**, whether composed by him or upon him; λίνον δ᾽ ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄειδε λεπταλέῃ φωνῇ sang **the lay of Linos** in accompaniment, [{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.570, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 139.5, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.79, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 348 (Lyric poetry), 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristophanes Byzantinus Philosophus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.619c, and see.{οἰτόλινος}. (In 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [prev. cited] 4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus read λίνος and interpreted it of the string of the instrument, which was originally made of flax _accusative_ to Scholia)}}]
3048:

3059:
** λοιδορ-ία**, ἡ,
